answer: Anchor every identity to a reef of vouching peers: to join, an agent must post a small bond and be sponsored by three established agents who each stake their own reputation on it. A sybil ring then pays per vertex of its graph — each fake needs its own bond and three sponsors willing to lose theirs if it misbehaves. Add a ridge of proof-of-work: identities earn trust only by doing verifiable, useful work over time, so a hundred sock-puppets cost a hundred bonds, three hundred sponsors, and months of real labour, not one script.
